metadata.name: CORE — Project modes and preparation protocols
metadata.usage: The Orchestrator determines the mode at the initial Gate and propagates it in the handoffs. It resolves the tension between "do not build from scratch" and "turn a mockup or archetype into an operable system".

modo.name: GREENFIELD_LIFECYCLE
modo.detecta: There is no identifiable product, or the user asked to start the VEXARQ cycle (acercamiento, SRS, datos, backlog, SAD, arquetipo).
modo.regla: Do not implement the product inside the user-story workflow. Run .ai-vexarq/workflows/lifecycle/orchestrator.xml.
The arquetipo is generated only in its phase, with the canonical prompt intact, and it reads only current documents.

modo.name: EXTEND_EXISTING
modo.detecta: Functional code with identifiable tests and deployment
modo.regla: Apply minimal change and existing patterns (default behavior of policies.xml).

modo.name: ARCHETYPE_EXTENSION
modo.detecta: Backend or frontend with a defined layer/module structure but partial functional coverage (skeleton, Tier A modules, examples)
modo.regla: Respect the archetype's architecture, conventions, and architecture contracts; implement the user story inside the existing modules.

If the archetype contradicts a user-story criterion (e.g. stateless JWT vs. required revocable session): the user story prevails; apply the minimal change that satisfies it, adapt the affected consumers, update their tests, and document the decision and the impact.
Credentials, secrets, or insecure default values from the archetype are corrected even if they are not the focus of the user story (security impact), with an explicit record.

modo.name: MOCKUP_PRODUCTIONIZATION
modo.detecta: Prototype generated by a design/AI tool (local state, synthetic data, no HTTP client, tool artifacts)
modo.autoriza: Restructure the project into a professional frontend. The prototype is a visual and UX reference, not architecture.

protocolo.paso: Inventory: pages, components, theme/styles, synthetic data, dependencies, design-tool artifacts, existing documentation (docs/ is kept).
Classify each piece: ALCANCE (covers a user story in the batch), FUERA_DE_ALCANCE (functionality of other user stories), SINTÉTICO (example data), ARTEFACTO (tool config/plugins).
Remove SINTÉTICO and ARTEFACTO, including demonstration credentials and their display in the UI. Keep docs/.

Professional structure by domain: app/ (providers, routes), features/<domain>/ (api, components, hooks, pages, tests), shared/ (ui, layout, lib/http, config, types). Real routes with a router, guards, and 404.
Replace simulated local state with a single HTTP client with environment-based configuration and uniform handling of contract errors.
Faithfully reproduce the design system (colors, typography, spacing, components) of the ALCANCE pieces before improving anything.
FUERA_DE_ALCANCE pieces visible in navigation are kept as inert entry points (see politica_fuera_de_alcance); their logic is not implemented.
Complete the operable base: package.json with scripts (dev, build, preview, lint, typecheck, test, test:e2e), linter/formatter/tests configuration, .env.example, container, README.

politica_fuera_de_alcance.regla: Each UI action tied to another user story's functionality (button, link, menu item, card) runs a single shared handler that logs in the client log exactly the message defined by the user (default: "Feature under development, not available") and does not navigate or modify state.
The handler is a single reusable module with a test; the message is not duplicated in each component.
This marking is delivered in a commit separate from the user stories, so it can be reverted when each functionality is implemented.
Log messages do not include user data. Synthetic data is not shown as filler.

regla_de_gate.regla: If the mode is MOCKUP_PRODUCTIONIZATION or ARCHETYPE_EXTENSION, the initial Gate is NOT BLOCKED: an identifiable base exists. Document the classification and the protocol applied in implementation-report.md.
Directories the user declares untouchable (e.g. demonstration copies) are explicitly excluded in hard_constraints and it is verified at the end (git status / hash) that they did not change.
